headline: Council to weigh ethics training for Councilor Wayne Mallar, warming shelter funding, and a homelessness communications plan.
summary: The workshop covers a recommended ethics training for Councilor Wayne Mallar, funding for warming shelters, and a communications plan recommendation from the Advisory Committee on Homelessness. The council will also meet in executive session to discuss legal matters related to Bangor Mall.

MEMORANDUM 
To: Bangor City Council 
From: Advisory Committee on Racial Equity, Inclusion, and Human Rights (ACREIHR) 
Date: October 9, 2026 
Re: Recommended Ethics Training for Councilor Wayne Mallar 
Purpose 
In response to the Ethics Committee's ﬁnding concerning Councilor Wayne Mallar and Section 33-5.1, 
Unbiased Conduct , the Advisory Committee on Racial Equity, Inclusion, and Human Rights has reviewed 
educational opportunities intended to address cultural awareness, bias, and ethical conduct in public 
service. 
Our recommendations prioritize meaningful learning, personal reﬂection, and practical application, with 
particular attention to the responsibilities of elected officials serving diverse communities. 
Primary Recommendation: Cross Cultural Community Services (CCCS) 
ACREIHR recommends a customized training facilitated by Cross Cultural Community Services 
(CCCS), a Maine-based organization specializing in cultural competency, equity, and inclusive practices. 
CCCS offers tailored educational programs that encourage participants to examine personal 
assumptions, recognize the inﬂuence of bias, and develop skills for respectful engagement across 
cultural differences. 
We believe an interactive, facilitated training would provide the greatest opportunity for meaningful 
reﬂection and learning directly applicable to Councilor Mallar's responsibilities as an elected official. 
Proposed Training Details: 
• Provider: Cross Cultural Community Services (CCCS)
• Format: Customized, facilitated training
• Recommended Duration: 90 minutes to 3 hours
• Cost: $350 per hour
• Estimated Total: $525–$1,050
The Committee is working with CCCS staff to determine the appropriate duration and content to ensure 
the training addresses the concerns identiﬁed in the Ethics Committee's ﬁndings. 
Website: https://www.crossculturalcommunityservices.org/ 
Secondary Recommendation: Creighton University 
As an alternative, ACREIHR recommends relevant courses offered through Creighton University's 
Lifelong Learning programs, particularly its Inclusion and Belonging offerings.
Creighton provides online, self-paced educational opportunities addressing cultural humility, implicit 
bias, personal awareness, and inclusive leadership. 
Relevant courses include: 
• Cultural Humility: Developing self-awareness, accountability, and respect across cultural
differences.
• Perceptions in Practice: Examining how assumptions and perceptions inﬂuence behavior and
decision-making.
• Perspective Taking: Strengthening the ability to understand differing experiences and viewpoints.
• Belonging vs. Not Belonging: Recognizing how language and behavior contribute to inclusion or
exclusion.
These courses offer structured learning with documented completion through individual course 
credentials. Courses may also contribute toward Creighton's broader certiﬁcate programs, subject to 
program requirements. 
Should this alternative be selected, the Committee recommends identifying speciﬁc courses that 
collectively address the Ethics Committee's ﬁndings and require documentation of successful 
completion. 
Website: https://lifelong.creighton.edu/browse/leadership-management/inclusion-and-belonging 
Committee Recommendation 
ACREIHR recommends the customized training offered by Cross Cultural Community Services as the 
preferred option. We believe facilitated discussion, individualized instruction, and opportunities for 
reﬂection provide the strongest foundation for addressing the concerns identiﬁed in the Ethics 
Committee's ﬁndings. 
The Committee recognizes the value of accessible, self-directed learning and offers Creighton University 
as a credible alternative. 
Ultimately, our recommendation is intended to support meaningful education and reinforce the 
standards of unbiased conduct, cultural awareness, and respectful public service expected of Bangor's 
elected officials.
Je nnifer Gunderman, Director

To: City Council 
From: Jennifer Gunderman, Director Public Health and Community Services 
Date: October 14, 2026 
RE: Warming Shelter Proposal & Financial Support 
Starting in November two warming shelters plan to start operations and one shelter plans to expand the number 
of beds. With support from MaineHousing funding, Bangor Area Homeless Shelter will offer five additional 
beds and The Brick Church will have up to sixty-five beds available each night. While the Mansion Church did 
not receive MaineHousing funds, they plan to open and offer up to twenty-five beds each night. 
Accumulatively, this totals up to ninety-five warming shelter beds a night.  
Based on a sample of data from the 2025-2026 Bangor warming shelter operations, an average of eighty-five 
people stayed in warming shelters. On twenty evenings, over ninety people were in warming shelters and on 
eleven days over one hundred people. With approximately 50-60 nights at 15 degrees or colder, there is a need 
for additional warming shelter space on those evenings. 
Bangor Public Health and Community Services (BPH&CS) is proposing that a warming shelter open on an as-
needed basis determined by weather criteria. Using the MaineHousing average cost per bed for up to sixty 
nights, the total cost for operating an as-needed warming shelter is estimated to be $106,000. This cost includes 
staff, utilities, cleaning, and other supplies. Together Place is interested and best prepared to offer this as-needed 
warming shelter.  Potential sources of funding include heating assistance funding administered by BPH&CS 
($5,000), GA reimbursement (approximately $11,000), and Community Development Block grant ($90,000).  
In addition, during a previous conversation, City Council agreed to support The Manna’s request of $7,000 and 
The Well’s request of $15,000 with non-opioid settlement funds. CDBG has been determined to be the most 
appropriate source of funding. Manna would be eligible for CDBG if repairs are not complete. 
Staff are seeking direction from Council and will be present to answer questions.
Carollynn J. Lear

OFFICE OF THE CITY MANAGER 
 
To: City Council 
From: Carollynn Lear, City Manager 
Date: September 14, 2026 
RE: Advisory Committee on Homelessness – First Recommendation  
 
The Advisory Committee on Homelessness has been meeting regularly on the second and fourth Tuesday 
of each month since their inaugural meeting in July. At the Committee’s August 25 th meeting, the 
Committee discussed issues around public -facing communication with a focus on how the City 
communicates about homelessness. The Committee noted that there is a lot of misinformation surrounding 
the topic of homelessness within the City , including a lot of inaccurate or incomplete information about 
what the City is doing to address the issue. The result of this discussion was a unanimous recommendation 
from the Advisory Committee that the City should formalize and effectuate a communications plan on the 
topic of homelessness with a focus on the following four areas: 
 
1. What the City is doing to address homelessness; 
 
2. Regular updates on the work of the Advisory Committee; 
 
3. Highlighting success stories; and 
 
4. Informing the public on how to get help with common issues or challenges related to homelessness.  
 
This recommendation is highly aligned with conversations and decisions that Council has already had 
around the importance of communication to the public about City operations. As we have previously 
discussed, recent structural changes in the City Manager’s Office have been made to create space for staff 
to focus more purposefully on communications and staff are currently formalizing a communications plan. 
We believe that this recommendation f its nicely with and should be integral part of that plan. However, 
appreciating that the Committee is Advisory in nature, we are seeking your input and approval of this 
recommendation before adopting it.
